content.content:
## Add a new setting

1. `Models/ClaudeCodeModels.cs` — add the property to the settings class with its default.
   Defaults must match what a fresh install should do; the JSON is merged over them.
2. Surface it — `ClaudeCodeControl.SettingsDialog.cs` (pick the right tab) or the ⚙ menu.
3. Apply it on load in `ClaudeCodeControl.Settings.cs` (`LoadSettings()` re-runs, so make the
   apply idempotent).
4. `ARCHITECTURE.md` → *Data Models & Settings* — add it to the Key settings list with its
   default and a one-line description.

Persistence is JSON at `%LocalAppData%\ClaudeCodeExtension\claudecode-settings.json` via
Newtonsoft.Json. Note that `SaveSettings()` deliberately preserves provider/model/effort fields
from disk during normal operation so parallel VS instances don't clobber each other — if your
setting is per-instance selection state, follow that pattern.

---

## Add a new UI file

**XAML control** — both files go in `UI/`, and the csproj needs two entries:

```xml
<Page Include="UI\Foo.xaml">
  <Generator>MSBuild:Compile</Generator>
  <SubType>Designer</SubType>
</Page>
...
<Compile Include="UI\Foo.xaml.cs">
  <DependentUpon>Foo.xaml</DependentUpon>
</Compile>
```

**Partial class of `ClaudeCodeControl`** — goes in `Controls/`, named
`ClaudeCodeControl.<Area>.cs`, plus a plain `<Compile Include="...">` entry.

Every `.cs` file needs the copyright header:

```csharp
/* ***********************
 * Application: ClaudeCodeExtension
 * Autor:  Daniel Carvalho Liedke / Claude Code
 * Copyright © Daniel Carvalho Liedke 2026
 * Usage and reproduction in any manner whatsoever without the written permission of Daniel Carvalho Liedke is strictly forbidden.
 * Purpose: <description>
 * ***********************/
```

Namespaces: `ClaudeCodeVS` for controls/models, `ClaudeCodeExtension` for the package.

---

## Localize chat text

Scope (v270.0): the whole extension — chat tab, panel, menus, toolbar, Settings and other dialogs,
message boxes, the Code Changes and Claude Usage windows. Model names, effort levels and provider
names stay as the CLIs spell them.

1. Write the English text wrapped: `L("Turn interrupted.")`, `L("Done in {0}", d)` (formats with
   the chat language's culture), XAML `{local:Loc 'Jump to the latest message'}` (escape `'` as `\'`).
   Static lists translated when shown: mark entries `N("...")`, call `L(entry)` at display time.
   Needs `using static ClaudeCodeVS.UI.Loc;`.
2. Never wrap text sent to the agent/CLI, slash commands, tool/provider/model names, log text or
   strings the code compares.
3. Translate it in **every** `lang/*.json` (19 files) in the same change — new, reworded or removed
   text alike. Keep the `{n}` placeholders, any leading/trailing space and a leading icon (`🤖 `,
   `■ `). `test.cmd` fails on a string missing from any file, on a translation whose English is gone
   from the code, on duplicate keys, empty values and on those three rules.
4. New built-in language: add it to `Loc.BuiltInLanguages` (code = .NET culture name, display name in
   that language), add `lang/<code>.json` with every key and an `<EmbeddedResource>` line in the
   csproj next to the others; the tests check the three agree. For a local fix or an extra language
   without a rebuild, drop the file in `%LocalAppData%\ClaudeCodeExtension\lang` (it also
   overrides embedded entries).
5. Text set from code after the XAML is built does not follow a language switch on its own: make
   sure `RefreshChatLanguage()` (or the view's `RefreshLanguage()`) redoes it. A tool window that
   lives outside the panel subscribes to `Loc.LanguageChanged` itself (Code Changes, Claude Usage).
   A modeless window built in code is retranslated in place with `UI.LocTree.Retranslate(window)`
   from `RefreshChatLanguage()` (GitHub Issues). Modal dialogs and menus built when opened need nothing.

---

## Pre-flight gates

    data = json.loads(raw)
    assert K1 not in data and K2 not in data
    lines = raw.split("\n")

        newline = "  " + json.dumps(k, ensure_ascii=False) + ": " + json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False) + ","
        # insert before first key line whose key sorts after k (ordinal)
        idx = None
        for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
            s = ln.strip()
            if not s.startswith('"'): continue
            key = json.loads("{" + s.rstrip(",") + "}")

            if key > k: idx = i; break

        lines.insert(idx, newline)

content.content: 937:Key settings: `SplitterPosition` (236px default), `SendWithEnter` (default true), `SendWithCtrlEnter` (default false — when true and `SendWithEnter` false, Ctrl+Enter sends and Enter inserts a newline; issue #70), `SendButtonInToolbar` (default false, v311.0 — Settings → Prompt, under "Button only"; the panel's ▶ Send sits in the toolbar strip left of 📎 instead of the prompt box corner), `SendSelectionReferenceOnly` (default false — Settings → Prompt; "Send Selection" inserts only the file path and line numbers, no code), `DisableClipboardSend` (default false — never paste: the prompt goes to a temp file and a short reference is typed with `SendInput`; Command Prompt only; issue #61), `SelectedProvider`, `VisibleProviders` (defaults to `[ClaudeCode]` — controls which agents appear in the provider menu; active provider is always shown regardless), `VisibleToolbarButtons` (`List<ToolbarButton>`, default `[RestartAgent, SessionHistory]` since v280.0 — features promoted to one-click toolbar buttons, the rest stay in ☰ Tools; see *Configurable Toolbar Buttons*), `ShowToolsMenuButton` (default true, v280.0 — Settings → Toolbar; hidden, unpromoted features are unreachable), `SessionHistoryButtonMigrated` (one-time flag, v280.0 — Session History promoted once when the composer's 🕘 merged into it), `ToolbarButtonOrder` (`List<ToolbarButton>`, default empty — the user's order for the toolbar and ☰ Tools (since v280.0 it also places ☰ ⚡ ⚙); `GetEffectiveToolbarOrder` completes empty/partial lists with the default order), `ToolbarButtonsRightAligned` (default false — Settings → Terminal since v291.0 (was Toolbar), under the prompt panel position; a strip narrower than its row sits at the right edge, the pre-v177 look; panel toolbar only — the chat tab's composer does not read it. Since v291.0 both ◀/▶ arrow slots collapse while nothing scrolls, so the strip sits flush against its aligned edge; the left slot used to stay Hidden and read as a gap before the first button), `SelectedClaudeModel`, `SelectedDevinModel` (string — the chosen Devin `model_uid`, shared by Devin (WSL) and Devin (native); empty = Devin's own default), `FavoriteDevinModels` (`List<string>` — Devin models starred as favorites, most recently starred first, uncapped; feeds the model menu's shortcuts and the picker's "Favorites"; v168.0, replaced the automatic `RecentDevinModels` MRU list), `SelectedProviderModels` (`Dictionary<string,string>` keyed by `AiProvider.ToString()` — the chosen model for every other agent; empty value = the agent's default) and `ModelCatalogs` (`Dictionary<string,ModelCatalogCache>` — the lists read from each CLI, 24h TTL; see *Model Catalog & Selection*), `PromptHistory` (max 50), `KeepLastPromptVisible` (default false — Settings → Prompt; the last prompt sent from the panel is laid over the empty prompt box as a dimmed, hit-test-invisible `LastPromptHint` TextBlock, set from `AddToPromptHistory` and re-evaluated on every `PromptTextBox` text change; in memory only, display only, never sent; issue #201), `AutoOpenChangesOnPrompt`, `PendingReviewEnabled` (default false — "Track agent changes for review (Keep/Undo)"; see *Pending Review*), `ChangesViewPendingScope` (default true — last scope chosen in the Changes view when pending review is on: pending list vs all uncommitted), `ClaudeDangerouslySkipPermissions`, `CodexFullAuto`, `CursorAgentAutoRun`, `DevinDangerousMode`, `AntigravityDangerouslySkipPermissions`, `QwenCodeYoloMode`, `GrokAlwaysApprove` (default false — `--always-approve` for Grok in terminal and native mode), `SelectedEffortLevel`, `SelectedCodexReasoningLevel` (default `Default` — Codex `model_reasoning_effort`, left to the model), `CustomWorkingDirectory` (global fallback) and `ProjectWorkingDirectories` (`Dictionary<string,string>` keyed by solution name — per-solution override that wins over it; issue #100), `SelectedTerminalType`, `ConsoleFontFaceName` (default `Cascadia Mono`) / `ConsoleFontSizePt` (default 0 = the terminal's own size; Ctrl+Scroll adjusts from it), `IsTerminalDetached`, `PromptFontSize` (8–24pt), `InvertLayout`, `SelectedLayoutOrientation` (default `Horizontal` — with `InvertLayout` it puts the prompt panel Top/Bottom/Left/Right; Settings → Layout), `HidePromptPanel` (default false — collapses the prompt text box, terminal reclaims the space; controls row/⚙ menu stay reachable to toggle back; ignored in native mode), `AutoHidePromptInNativeMode` (default true — collapses the panel prompt box while the native chat is in its own tab, whose composer replaces it; ignored while the chat is docked in the panel; issue #151), `AutoHidePanelInNativeMode` (default true — hides the whole panel once the native chat is on screen in its own tab; v258.0), `ChatIconStyle` (default Classic — Modern: VS icons on the chat toolbar, ring spinner, colored tab status), `ChatWorkingTabIcon` (default Clock — Modern working tab icon: Arrows, Clock, Moon), `ShowChatTokenCounts` (default true — token counts in the live status and the turn footer), `ExpandFailedToolCalls` (default true — a failed tool call opens its card by itself; v276.0), `ReturnToPlanModeAfterPlan` (default true — Settings → Automation; a Claude native chat goes back to Plan mode after the turn that carried out an approved plan; off keeps the approved mode for the conversation; v316.0, #268), `ChatThinkingDisplay` (default `Collapsed` — `Collapsed` / `OpenBeforeQuestion` / `AlwaysOpen`: which thinking rows the native chat opens by itself; Settings → Native mode; see *Native Mode* → thinking rows), `ChatTabsInOneWindow` (default false — every native chat as a tab of one remembered window, applied after a restart; see *All chats in one window*; v276.0), `ReopenChatTabsWithSolution` (default false — reopen the native chat tabs per workspace; see *Reopening chat tabs with the solution*; replaced the v263.0 `ReopenChatTabsOnSolutionOpen`, default true, in v277.0 — `DropRetiredReopenChatTabsSetting` removes the old key from `AdditionalData` once and clears `WorkspaceChatTabs`, so every install starts with it off) / `WorkspaceChatTabs` (the saved lists), `CompactChatToolbar` (default false — chat toolbar inside the message box), `WelcomeCardContent` (default `RecentAndTips` — what a new chat's welcome card shows: `Nothing`, `TipsOnly`, `RecentOnly`, `RecentAndTips`), `PlainChatWorkingStatus` (default false — live status always "Thinking…" instead of rotating verbs; pushed to the static `ChatTranscriptView.PlainWorkingStatus` on load and on Settings OK), `ChatLanguage` (default "auto" — chat UI language: VS UI language, "en", or a culture with a lang file), `ShowChatTabStatus` / `AutoTitleChatTabs` / `AutoTitleChatTabsWithAi` (all default true — chat tab status glyph, automatic tab title from the first prompt, AI title via a low-cost model for Claude Code; v259.0), `SelectedThemePreference` (Automatic/Dark/Light/Custom), `CustomThemeColorArgb` (bg color for Custom, default #F4ECFF), `LastAgentTerminalColorArgb` (agent's launched color, skips redundant restart prompts), `SkipThemeRestartPrompt` (default false), `DefaultNativeSessionColor` (`"#RRGGBB"`, empty = built-in blue `#1C8AE0` — Settings → Appearance → Native Color Schema; fallback for native sessions with no entry in `SessionTitleColors`, resolved in `GetNativeSessionColor`; applying it live-refreshes open chats), `CustomCommands` (list of `{Name, Command}`), `UsageAutoRefreshSeconds` (0 = manual), `UsageWindowOpened` (auto-reopen on load), `ShowInlineUsageBars` (default true), `ShowSubagentCount` (default false — live running-subagent count in the panel toolbar, Claude Code only; content.content:
## Ship a release

**Mandatory for every session that modifies code.** Bump the MAJOR by one, minor always `.0`
(176.0 → 177.0). Do not resume 10.x-style minor bumps.

1. `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs` — `AssemblyVersion` **and** `AssemblyFileVersion` to `177.0.0.0`
   (both, four parts).
2. `source.extension.vsixmanifest` — `Version="177.0"` in the `<Identity>` tag (two parts).
3. `README.md` — add `### Version 177.0` at the top of `## Version History`.

**Verify:** `./test.cmd`. `VersionConsistencyTests` makes this rule executable — it asserts
`AssemblyVersion == AssemblyFileVersion`, that the short form matches the manifest and the
newest README heading, and that the minor is `.0`. A missed file fails the suite, and
`publish.cmd` runs it as a gate.

**Release-note style** (README only — the one section where prose discipline matters):

- Short and business-focused. One sentence per bullet, two max.
- Describe the user-visible feature or fix, not the implementation.
- Avoid: code/file/class/method names, internal selectors, paths, constants, line numbers,
  JS snippets, framework jargon (`CoreWebView2`, `INPUT_RECORD`, `NavigationCompleted`),
  step-by-step "how it works", PR-style root-cause analysis.
- Keep: what the user gets ("auto-confirms proxy block screens"), opt-in/opt-out status, and
  the menu or setting name they interact with.
- Technical detail belongs in the commit message and `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

**Other README sections** (Features, Supported AI Providers, System Requirements, Settings &
Menus…): edit the exact line affected and nothing else. New provider → one row. Reworded
feature → one word. Do not rewrite paragraphs, add subsections, reorder, or restructure
tables. README is reference doc; keep it slim.

---

## Publish

Any phrasing — "publish the app", "publish to marketplace", "ship it" — means one thing:

```bash
./publish.cmd    # from the repo root
```

Do **not** invoke MSBuild or marketplace APIs by hand; `publish.cmd` is the authoritative
automation. It runs `test.cmd` → Clean → Rebuild Release → publish the VSIX through
`VsixPublisher.exe` with `publishManifest.json`, falling back from VS 2026 to VS 2022 tool
paths. Success is detected via the `VsixPub0038` log marker, which works around the
VsixPublisher telemetry crash in VS 18.

`publishManifest.json` holds the marketplace metadata: publisher `dliedke`, category `coding`,
free, Q&A enabled, README.md as the overview.

Publishing is outward-facing and hard to reverse — confirm with the user before running it
unless they just asked for it.

---
